title: POC weekly runbook & SDK integration sync
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on runbook for SDK integration, function-calling behavior, structured output contracts and security requirements. SE demoed updated SDK sample with retry/backoff and a small fallback to a lighter quantized variant. Customer raised concerns around audit logs, SSO, and deterministic output for downstream order processing. Agreed next steps: share runbook draft, schedule a dedicated latency benchmark, and deliver security pack and sample code for on-prem/VPC test.
topics: Function / tool calling reliability and fallbacks
Structured JSON output contract and validation
Benchmark plan: latency and token cost targets

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-14 | 10:00 AM PT | 46 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Ben Vargas (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (AtlasCommerce - Lead Engineer), Marcus Li (Product), Elena Gomez (Security)
[00:00] Alice: Hey everyone thanks for jumping on, quick agenda — runbook review, SDK sample, function-calling reliability and then security questions. how's timing for people?
[00:18] Priya: good, thanks. we did a quick smoke on the SDK you sent last week, a couple of things showed up when we did high concurrency, we'll show logs in a bit.
[00:32] Ben: yeah i pushed a small update to the sample yesterday — added retry + exponential backoff and a simple local cache for prefix calls, because we saw cold-starts spike. not a full KV cache but it helps.
[00:48] Marcus: one ask from product side — we need the structured output to be stable, we feed directly into our order processor. small schema drift kills the pipeline.
[01:05] Priya: exact, the example returned a "customer_address" as string once and then split into object next run, so our parser failed.
[01:22] Ben: okay that sounds like a templating prompt issue, when function-calling is enabled the model sometimes writes freeform instead of strict JSON. in the SDK sample i added a function schema wrapper that forces JSON, but it's not perfect. we can add JSON-schema validation in the client to catch this before ingestion.
[01:38] Elena: also from security — where are logs stored, do we have audit trails for each token and who can read them? we have compliance windows and need that spelled out.
[01:50] Alice: yep, good question. Redwood's hosted option keeps audit logs in the control plane, can parcel them to your S3, and we support encryption via KMS. for dedicated/private we'll provide customer-managed KMS and longer retention. we'll send the security pack.
[02:06] Priya: can you clarify the fallback you mentioned? we want graceful degradation if the main model times out.
[02:15] Ben: approach is two-tiered — primary hosted model with our latency SLOs, and a fallback smaller quantized variant pinned in the SDK. the SDK sample includes a quick switch: if request latency > threshold or error rate spikes, client falls back to quantized stub. that reduces token quality but keeps pipeline moving.
[02:33] Marcus: cost vs quality tradeoff — product prefers consistent latency even if occasional lower quality, but ops prefers to avoid noisy outputs.
[02:44] Priya: our success criteria for pilot is 99% of calls succeed end-to-end and parsing errors <0.5% over 48 hours.
[02:56] Alice: noted, we'll make those the acceptance criteria in the runbook.
[03:10] Ben: i want to demo the SDK run locally — small screen share — (quiet typing / demo)
[03:40] Speaker 1: (screen share) showing repo layout: /examples/order_ingest, run.sh, retry logic in client.js, function schema file.
[04:05] Ben: the main trick is function calling with a schema that enforces types. we still saw one case where the model emitted an extra field "delivery_notes" as null and their parser complained. so client-level sanitization needed.
[04:29] Priya: can the SDK auto-strip unknown fields? that would be huge.
[04:35] Ben: yes we can add an option to drop unknown keys or map them to a metadata bag. we'll add that to the sample as a toggle.
[05:00] Elena: for SSO — we need SAML2 support and role-based access for the console, plus audit events forwarded to our SIEM.
[05:12] Alice: Redwood supports SAML SSO for enterprise, RBAC on console and API keys, and we can forward logs to your SIEM via webhook or S3 ingestion. we'll include docs.
[05:28] Marcus: about private deployment — being realistic, we may start on hosted then move to dedicated capacity or VPC if latency or data policies demand it. timeline wise, product wants a pilot in prod-ish staging by mid-June.
[05:42] Alice: that's doable if benchmarks are good; we should run a dedicated latency run next week to validate.
[06:00] Ben: quick note on tokenization costs — when you switch to quantized models token counts can change slightly, so cost curves will differ. i'll add estimates to the runbook.
[06:15] Priya: on the concurrency issue we saw 429s at 120 rps, even after the SDK retries some requests failed with mismatched session state. could that be KV cache misrouting?
[06:30] Ben: possibly — we have to ensure KV cache affinity is preserved per session. i suspect the sample's local cache wasn't using the session id consistently. i'll fix that.
[06:44] Priya: great. we'll also reproduce and attach logs.
[07:00] Ben: another resiliency pattern — request hedging: send a duplicate to a lower-cost region after X ms. it's a heavier cost pattern but keeps p99 low. do you want us to include hedging as an option?
[07:15] Marcus: not by default, maybe toggled for high-value transactions only.
[07:25] Alice: we'll document hedging in the runbook and leave default off.
[07:36] Priya: about structured output — we want a signed schema and strict validation. can Redwood's SDK do pre-flight validation and reject before backfilling?
[07:49] Ben: yes we can run a JSON-schema check client-side and also ask the model to adhere to a "response_schema" via function-calling. sometimes the model invents fields though, so we'll log and optionally auto-strip.
[08:05] Elena: please include the retention period for those validation logs, because compliance might require 1 year.
[08:16] Alice: we'll include retention options and costs. default hosted retention is 90 days, dedicated can be extended.
[08:30] (Brief silence / typing)
[08:50] Priya: on the code sample, i noticed the retry backoff didn't persist the partial KV state if restart happened. that's why some calls read stale memory.
[09:05] Ben: aha — we can persist to a lightweight redis in your staging env. the sample can include instructions. that would maintain cache across restarts.
[09:20] Priya: that helps. also if we run on VPC/on-prem we'll need a connector to your control plane — how intrusive is that?
[09:32] Alice: for private we ship a control-plane agent that runs on your VPC and talks back over TLS, you keep keys. it's a one-time setup. we'll add runbook steps.
[09:45] Marcus: ok, timeline check — what are the near-term deliverables from Redwood?
[09:52] Alice: runbook draft, sample updates (fallback, strip unknown keys), security pack, and propose benchmark times.
[10:02] Priya: and we'll run sample, share logs and security questions.
[10:10] Ben: quick callout — i added a small test harness in the repo to simulate race conditions and token variations; we'll point you to it.
[10:24] Elena: any blockers on SOC2 artifacts? we need the scope and mapper for ingestion.
[10:32] Alice: we have a SOC2 pack that lists controls and evidence types. we'll send it and schedule a short compliance call if needed.
[10:44] Marcus: sounds good. one last product note — can you include a tiny A/B plan in the runbook so we can compare quality between primary and quantized fallback?
[10:55] Ben: yep i'll add an A/B test guide and metrics to capture — parsing errors, p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens, and subjective quality score.
[11:08] Alice: great. let's recap next steps quickly.
[11:15] (Recap)
[11:20] Alice: Ben will update sample and add unknown-key toggle, add fallback snippet, and bench harness link. Ben due May 18.
[11:29] Alice: i'll send runbook and pricing on May 17.
[11:34] Priya: i'll run in staging and file any parsing failures by May 20.
[11:40] Elena: i'll send SOC2 scope questions by May 19.
[11:45] Alice: ok thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and schedule the benchmark sesh next week.
[11:52] (Meeting ends)
